theory.title: Oraciones de relativo con whose, where y when
theory.explanation: Usa whose para expresar posesión («cuyo/a»), where para referirte a un lugar («donde») y when para referirte a un momento («cuando»). Estas palabras unen ideas y evitan repetir un sustantivo: a village where people still speak the local language (un pueblo donde todavía se habla la lengua local).
theory.tip: Whose = cuyo/a; where = donde; when = cuando.

patterns.label: Oraciones de relativo con whose, where y when · 1
patterns.pattern: I met a woman whose family has lived here for generations.
examples:
I met a woman whose family has lived here for generations.
→ Conocí a una mujer cuya familia vive aquí desde hace generaciones.

patterns.label: Oraciones de relativo con whose, where y when · 2
patterns.pattern: This is the village where my grandparents grew up.
examples:
This is the village where my grandparents grew up.
→ Este es el pueblo donde crecieron mis abuelos.

patterns.label: Oraciones de relativo con whose, where y when · 3
patterns.pattern: I remember the year when we first visited.
examples:

→ Recuerdo el año en que lo visitamos por primera vez.

patterns.label: Oraciones de relativo con whose, where y when · 4
patterns.pattern: They visited a school whose students speak three languages.
examples:
They visited a school whose students speak three languages.
→ Visitaron una escuela cuyos alumnos hablan tres idiomas.

patterns.label: Oraciones de relativo con whose, where y when · 5

patterns.label: Oraciones de relativo con whose, where y when · 7

examples:
We stayed with a family whose home was near the coast.

patterns.label: Oraciones de relativo con whose, where y when · 8

→ Este es el festival donde todo el mundo lleva ropa tradicional.

patterns.label: Oraciones de relativo con whose, where y when · 9
patterns.pattern: I remember a time when people exchanged letters.
examples:
I remember a time when people exchanged letters.
→ Recuerdo una época en la que la gente intercambiaba cartas.

patterns.label: Oraciones de relativo con whose, where y when · 10
patterns.pattern: The guide introduced an artist whose work is famous abroad.
examples:
The guide introduced an artist whose work is famous abroad.

content.passage: During a visit to a small town, I met a guide whose family had lived there for many years. She showed us the square where the local festival takes place. She also described the year when the tradition first began. We visited a school whose students learn several languages. The guide explained that the town is a place where different cultures meet and influence one another.

items.prompt: Describe a person whose work you admire.
items.modelAnswer: I admire a nurse who works at the local health centre. She is patient, explains things clearly and treats every person with respect. Her work makes a real difference to people in the community.

items.prompt: Talk about a place where people celebrate a tradition.
items.modelAnswer: I once visited a village where people celebrate the harvest with music, dancing and a shared meal. Families decorate the main square, and local producers sell their food. It is a tradition that brings generations together.

items.prompt: Describe a time when you learned something about another culture.
items.modelAnswer: During a trip to Morocco, I learned that it is polite to accept mint tea when a host offers it, even if you only drink a little. Sharing tea is an important part of welcoming guests.

items.prompt: Talk about a school whose students speak different languages.
items.modelAnswer: I know a school whose students speak several languages at home. The teachers encourage them to share words and stories from their cultures. It creates a friendly environment where differences are valued.

items.prompt: Describe a market where local people meet.
items.modelAnswer: The Saturday market is a place where local people meet to buy fruit, cheese and handmade products. It is also a good place to hear news and talk to neighbours. I enjoy the lively atmosphere.

items.prompt: Explain a moment when you felt welcome.
items.modelAnswer: I felt welcome when a family invited me to join their table during a local celebration. They explained the dishes and introduced me to their relatives. I was grateful that they included me.

items.prompt: Talk about a family whose traditions you find interesting.
items.modelAnswer: My friend's family has traditions that I find interesting. Every New Year's Day, they prepare a special meal and each person shares one hope for the coming year. It is a simple way to feel connected.

items.prompt: Describe a festival where visitors can learn about local culture.
items.modelAnswer: The spring festival is an event where visitors can learn about local music, food and crafts. There are workshops for children and demonstrations by local artists. It is both educational and enjoyable.

items.prompt: Remember a time when you travelled somewhere new.
items.modelAnswer: I remember travelling to a small town in the north where I didn't know anyone. I arrived late, but a shop owner helped me find my guesthouse. The experience reminded me that kindness can make a new place feel familiar.

items.prompt: Make sentences with whose, where and when.
items.modelAnswer: I admire a musician whose songs tell stories about her hometown. The village where she grew up holds a festival every summer, when visitors can hear traditional music. These clauses add useful information about people, places and times.

B: They showed respect and made new friendships.
